bull_bear.body:
- Flagship company of the TGV Group and the leading producer of Chlor-Alkali products, with a strong presence of four decades in the south Indian chemical industry
- Adopts bipolar membrane technology in its chlor-alkali operations
- Captive renewable power base — solar plus a wind farm at Ramagiri and a power plant at Bellary — being expanded to lower and stabilise energy cost
- Credit Rating of CARE A with Stable outlook for both long term and short term bank facilities, maintained unchanged
- Circular-economy integration: salt and acids reclaimed from waste water are used as raw materials in one of the group companies; recovered sodium sulphate and spent sulphuric acid are sold as products
- Member of the Executive Committee and the Technical Sub-Committee of the Alkali Manufacturers Association of India (AMAI)
- Diversified chemical portfolio where no single product beyond Caustic Soda (58% of turnover) dominates, with Caustic Potash (17%) and Methyl Chloride (12%) as further contributors
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material availability and prices — Management's Cautionary Statement names raw material availability and prices first among the important factors that could make actual results differ materially from stated expectations; the Company is a chlor-alkali producer dependent on salt, methanol and power inputs.
- Cyclical demand and pricing in principal markets — The Cautionary Statement explicitly flags cyclical demand and pricing in the Company's principal markets. Commodity chlor-alkali realisations swing with the cycle, and the AR itself notes that the year's favourable ratios were the result of better performance in main products — the same lever reverses in a downcycle.
- Regulatory and tax-regime change — Changes in Government regulations and tax regimes are named as factors that could materially change operating outcomes. As a hazardous-chemical manufacturer the Company is also subject to Extended Producer Responsibility obligations and Pollution Control Board plans.
- Macroeconomic exposure in India and export destinations — The Cautionary Statement cites economic developments within India and in the countries in which the Company conducts business; exports contribute 10% of turnover across 28 countries.
- Product concentration in Caustic Soda — Caustic Soda Lye/Flakes accounted for 58% of turnover in 2025-26 (61% and 60% in the two preceding years), with Caustic Potash at 17% and Methyl Chloride at 12%, and the Chemicals Segment as a whole at 98% of turnover — a single-product, single-segment concentration.
- Environmental and hazardous-materials exposure at a single main site — Manufacturing is concentrated at Gondiparla, Kurnool. BRSR identifies fossil-resource consumption, air pollution, resource loss and ground contamination as risks arising from methanol, methyl chloride, chloroform and hydrochloric acid production and disposal, mitigated through dyke-walled storage tanks and higher-capacity tanker exports. Hazardous brine sludge is disposed to the Company's own secured landfill within the premises.
- Related-party transaction concentration — BRSR discloses related parties at 27% of total investments and 5% of purchases in FY 2025-26 (34% and 8% respectively in FY 2024-25), with a long AOC-2 roster of group counterparties across sales, purchases, land, advisory and lease transactions — a governance and pricing-transparency exposure.
- Customer and dealer concentration and lengthening payables — Sales to dealers/distributors were 60.42% of total sales in FY 2025-26, with the top 10 dealers at 25.17%; days of accounts payable rose from 74 in FY 2024-25 to 98 in FY 2025-26, and purchases from trading houses moved from nil to 7.34% of total purchases.
- Product-quality specification gap in pharmaceutical-grade MDC — 1,1-dichloroethylene in the Methylene Dichloride stream currently tracks at 15-20 ppm against a customer specification requiring below 8 ppm; until R&D optimisation succeeds, supply into high-purity pharmaceutical applications remains closed to the Company.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: The Company manufactures Caustic Soda, Caustic Potash, Chlorine and Chloro methanes as its main products in the Chemicals Segment, and produces Castor Oil Derivatives, Soap Noodles, Hydroxy Stearic Acid and Glycerine in its Oils and Fats Segment. Its products are industrial inputs, so the majority of customers are industrial units and the company operates a B2B marketing model directly to industrial customers and through traders for other customers. Operations are run from a manufacturing complex at Gondiparla, Kurnool (A.P.) supported by captive wind and solar power assets.

outlook.body:
- Transition to clean energy through captive solar and wind generation, with more thrust given to solar power generation as it is eco-friendly and also leads to cost control and ensures sustainability
- Improve the credit rating further from the maintained CARE A / Stable on both long term and short term bank facilities
- Optimise process purification to cut 1,1-DCE in the Methylene Dichloride stream below pharmaceutical-grade thresholds so as to unlock supply capability into high-purity pharmaceutical applications
- Circular-economy operation: reclaim salt and acids from waste water for use as raw materials in a group company, recover sodium sulphate from brine by nano filtration for sale, and sell spent sulphuric acid as a by-product
- Raise productivity through in-house training and development programmes for all levels of employees, with occupational health, safety and environmental management given utmost importance
- Strengthen internal control through an internal audit programme oriented towards review of controls and operational improvements

outlook.body: The single named expansion project disclosed in this annual report is in captive renewable power: the BRSR capex disclosure states the year's capex was directed towards increasing the capacity of the solar power plant to 57.9 MW by installing an additional 20 MW on top of the existing 37.9 MW solar power plant. This sits alongside the Company's stated intent to give more thrust to solar power generation because it is eco-friendly and will lead to cost control and sustainability through use of renewable energy resources. The Company operates from three national plant locations - the chemical complex at Gondiparla, Kurnool (A.P.), the wind farm at Ramagiri, Anantapur Dist. (A.P.) and the Bellary power plant at Tagginabudihalli, Karnataka - plus one office, with no international sites. On the product side, R&D expenditure is being applied to optimise process purification parameters so as to bring 1,1-dichloroethylene in the Methylene Dichloride product stream from a current 15-20 ppm to below the 8 ppm pharmaceutical-grade specification, which the Company says would unlock supply capability for high-purity pharmaceutical applications. Separately, the Board has proposed a Special Resolution at the 44th AGM to alter the Memorandum of Association object clause to permit land development and a contracting, building, town-planning, infrastructure and estate-development business, and a further Special Resolution to increase the Company's borrowing powers in supersession of the limit set at the 32nd AGM in 2014. No rupee capex quantum is stated: the annual report's Capital Commitments note and the segment Capital Expenditure disclosure both arrive without a readable figure.

deepdive.thesis: TGV SRAAC Limited (formerly Sree Rayalaseema Alkalies and Allied Chemicals Ltd.) is the flagship company of the TGV Group and a leading producer of Chlor-Alkali products, with a presence of four decades in the south Indian chemical industry.

open.item: Board has recommended a final dividend of Rs.1 per equity share of Rs.10 each fully paid-up for the financial year ending March 31, 2026, for declaration at the 44th AGM.

Special Resolution proposed at the 44th AGM to alter the Object Clause of the Memorandum of Association to permit land acquisition/development and a contracting, building, town-planning, infrastructure and real-estate development business, signalling a potential new non-chemical vertical.
Special Resolution proposed at the 44th AGM under Section 180(1)(c) to increase the Board's borrowing powers, in supersession of the resolution passed at the 32nd AGM held on 25.09.2014.
Increase the capacity of the solar power plant to 57.9 MW by installing an additional 20 MW to the existing 37.9 MW solar power plant.
The Company is working in a direction to improve its credit rating beyond the maintained CARE A with Stable outlook on both long term and short term bank facilities.

Optimise process purification parameters to bring 1,1-dichloroethylene (1,1-DCE) in the Methylene Dichloride product stream below 8 ppm, from a current 15-20 ppm, to unlock supply into high-purity pharmaceutical applications.
Give more thrust to solar power generation, which is eco-friendly and will also lead to cost control and ensure sustainability through use of renewable energy resources.

Refine reaction/separation dynamics so that 1,1-dichloroethylene in the Methylene Dichloride product stream falls below the 8 ppm pharmaceutical-grade specification from a current 15-20 ppm, enabling full compliance with customer quality standards and unlocking supply into high-purity pharmaceutical applications.
Continue vendor audits, currently covering five major suppliers accounting for approximately 65% of inputs, extending awareness on quality, environment and safety at the pre-audit stage.
Life Cycle Perspective / Assessments on a cradle-to-gate boundary are in progress for the Company's product portfolio, with results not yet communicated in the public domain.

- Raw material availability and prices — Management's Cautionary Statement names raw material availability and prices first among the important factors that could make actual results differ materially from stated expectations; the Company is a chlor-alkali producer dependent on salt, methanol and power inputs.
- Cyclical demand and pricing in principal markets — The Cautionary Statement explicitly flags cyclical demand and pricing in the Company's principal markets. Commodity chlor-alkali realisations swing with the cycle, and the AR itself notes that the year's favourable ratios were the result of better performance in main products — the same lever reverses in a downcycle.
- Regulatory and tax-regime change — Changes in Government regulations and tax regimes are named as factors that could materially change operating outcomes. As a hazardous-chemical manufacturer the Company is also subject to Extended Producer Responsibility obligations and Pollution Control Board plans.
- Macroeconomic exposure in India and export destinations — The Cautionary Statement cites economic developments within India and in the countries in which the Company conducts business; exports contribute 10% of turnover across 28 countries.
- Product concentration in Caustic Soda — Caustic Soda Lye/Flakes accounted for 58% of turnover in 2025-26 (61% and 60% in the two preceding years), with Caustic Potash at 17% and Methyl Chloride at 12%, and the Chemicals Segment as a whole at 98% of turnover — a single-product, single-segment concentration.
- Environmental and hazardous-materials exposure at a single main site — Manufacturing is concentrated at Gondiparla, Kurnool. BRSR identifies fossil-resource consumption, air pollution, resource loss and ground contamination as risks arising from methanol, methyl chloride, chloroform and hydrochloric acid production and disposal, mitigated through dyke-walled storage tanks and higher-capacity tanker exports. Hazardous brine sludge is disposed to the Company's own secured landfill within the premises.
- Related-party transaction concentration — BRSR discloses related parties at 27% of total investments and 5% of purchases in FY 2025-26 (34% and 8% respectively in FY 2024-25), with a long AOC-2 roster of group counterparties across sales, purchases, land, advisory and lease transactions — a governance and pricing-transparency exposure.
- Customer and dealer concentration and lengthening payables — Sales to dealers/distributors were 60.42% of total sales in FY 2025-26, with the top 10 dealers at 25.17%; days of accounts payable rose from 74 in FY 2024-25 to 98 in FY 2025-26, and purchases from trading houses moved from nil to 7.34% of total purchases.
- Product-quality specification gap in pharmaceutical-grade MDC — 1,1-dichloroethylene in the Methylene Dichloride stream currently tracks at 15-20 ppm against a customer specification requiring below 8 ppm; until R&D optimisation succeeds, supply into high-purity pharmaceutical applications remains closed to the Company.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Transition to clean energy through captive solar and wind generation, with more thrust given to solar power generation as it is eco-friendly and also leads to cost control and ensures sustainability
- Improve the credit rating further from the maintained CARE A / Stable on both long term and short term bank facilities
- Optimise process purification to cut 1,1-DCE in the Methylene Dichloride stream below pharmaceutical-grade thresholds so as to unlock supply capability into high-purity pharmaceutical applications

hero.oneLiner: TGV SRAAC Limited (formerly Sree Rayalaseema Alkalies and Allied Chemicals Ltd.) is the flagship company of the TGV Group and a leading producer of Chlor-Alkali products, with a presence of four decades in the south Indian chemical industry.
